objective: Remove M127's row-mask priority-predecode cone from the weight-select critical path and eliminate its cross-row bubble by accepting one canonical K1-K4 descriptor per cycle.

motivation.m127_matched_dc_observation: At 3.000 ns, M127's worst path starts at row_source_mask, traverses canonical priority predecode, a 16:1 weight select and a pair add, then ends at pipe_pair_sum_q. Its setup slack is 0.1299 ns versus M125's 0.2488 ns.
motivation.repair: The sparse producer supplies an already canonical descriptor containing up to four distinct source IDs. M128 retains only descriptor audit, four weight selections, signed pair reduction and one elastic output stage.

architecture.elastic_behavior: one-entry signed pair-sum pipeline replaces its retiring entry on the same accepted cycle

paper_safe_statement: Commercial VCS verifies a descriptor-streamed signed K4 fold with one accepted descriptor per cycle across row boundaries, exact signed numeric results over 36,864 lanes, randomized output stalls and fail-closed descriptor/reset attacks. External descriptor generation, physical frequency and system speedup remain unadmitted.
prohibited_claims: Do not describe external canonical descriptor generation as free.
Do not claim bandwidth reduction; the current descriptor is 53 bits and has not been compared against a complete source format.
Do not claim frequency or physical speedup before matched Synopsys DC grid evidence and independent review.
Do not call the behavioral 1536-byte cache a foundry SRAM macro.
Do not multiply the M122 cycle projection by an unadmitted frequency ratio.
Do not claim end-to-end, system, energy or FPS improvement.
